seoTitle: Free DNS Zone Record Generator - BIND and Route 53
metaDescription: Write DNS records as simple lines and get a validated BIND zone file, Route 53 change batch or JSON. Supports A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, CAA. Free.
intro: Turns simple lines such as "MX @ 10 mail.example.com" into a validated BIND zone file, a Route 53 ChangeBatch JSON or a plain JSON list. Nothing is looked up or published.
why: Moving a domain or setting up mail usually means typing a dozen DNS records into a provider's form or zone file, where one wrong dot or missing quote breaks something quietly. This tool lets you write each record as a short line and checks it before producing output: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, MX priorities, SRV fields, CAA tags and hostnames are validated, long TXT values are split into 255-byte strings, and a CNAME that shares a name with other records is rejected. The output can be pasted into a BIND file or sent to Route 53 as a change batch. It is a writing aid, not a resolver, and it never contacts any DNS server.
howTo: Enter the zone, for example example.com, and the default TTL.
Write one record per line as TYPE name value, using @ for the apex and ttl=300 to override the TTL.
Choose BIND zone file, Route 53 ChangeBatch JSON or JSON list, then copy the output.

faq.a: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SRV, CAA and PTR. Any other type gives an error naming the line. Each type has its own validation, for example MX needs a priority and a target host.

faq.q: How are long TXT records handled?
faq.a: Values over 255 bytes are split into several quoted strings in one record, as DNS requires. This matters for DKIM keys and long SPF records.

faq.q: Why does it complain about a CNAME?
faq.a: DNS forbids a CNAME on a name that has any other record type. The tool checks this across your lines and stops with the name that conflicts.

faq.q: Does it check my live DNS or publish anything?
faq.a: No. It only formats and validates what you type. The SOA values in the BIND header are placeholders, so replace them with your provider's before loading the file.
